question.problem:
For the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ which of the following statements are true? 

I. $u$ is orthogonal to the set $V=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $u$ is orthogonal to the set $H=\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W=\{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $V,H$ and $W$ as $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},\{{h}_{1},{h}_{2}\}$ and $\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\}$, respectively. 

Now, we have to compute the dot product between $u$ and the vectors in each set. 

- For the set $V:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {v}_{1} & =2\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 5=19\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $u$ is not orthogonal to the set $V.$ Notice that we stopped after finding the first non-orthogonal vector in the set.

- For the set $H:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {h}_{1} & =2\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-4)+2\cdot (-1)=0,\,✓ \\ u\cdot {h}_{2} & =2\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-1)=-1\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

 
So, $u$ is not orthogonal to the set $H.$

- For the set $W:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1} & =2\cdot (-4)+(-1)\cdot (-6)+2\cdot 1=0\,✓ \\ u\cdot {w}_{2} & =2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-8)+2\cdot (-5)=0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
